walkthroughs.body_html: Diwali is a five-day Hindu festival of lights celebrated around October or November. It marks the return of Rama after defeating Ravana, and honours Lakshmi. Families light lamps (diyas), share sweets, give gifts and set off fireworks. Sikhs and Jains also celebrate.

Vesak (also Wesak) is the most important Buddhist festival. It celebrates the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death. Buddhists visit temples, meditate, give to charity and decorate with lanterns and flowers, usually on the full moon in May.

Vaisakhi is a Sikh festival on 13 or 14 April. It marks the day in 1699 when Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa, a community of committed Sikhs. There are processions, prayers and shared meals at the gurdwara.
